- **Soap** [`soap`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/soap.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Bodies are cleaned with oil and strigil, cloth with stale urine and fuller's earth. Tallow, olive oil, wood ash and lime are cheap. Fullers and bath keepers are the buyers. Local: fullers (fullones); bath keepers (balneatores). Elsewhere: Gaul, a tallow-and-ash hair pomade (reported by later Roman writers).
- **Distillation of strong alcohol (aqua vitae)** [`distillation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/distillation.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Aristotle notes that vapour from boiled sea water condenses fresh. No still exists. Coppersmiths and potters can build pot, head and tube; tight joints and cooling are the craft problems. Local: perfumers of the Seplasia at Capua; coppersmiths (aerarii); wine from Campania and Latium.
- **Sulphuric acid (oil of vitriol)** [`sulphuric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sulphuric_acid.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Green and blue vitriol (shoemakers' black, chalcanthum) and alum are traded goods; no one has distilled them. Needs retorts that survive red heat.
- **Oxygen and combustion** [`oxygen_combustion`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oxygen_combustion.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Fire is an element, or for Epicureans a swarm of fine atoms. A lamp dying under a jar is easily shown. Isolating the gas needs mercury calx and blown glass.
- **Nitric acid (aqua fortis)** [`nitric_acid`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/nitric_acid.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Needs saltpetre, vitriol and a still, none of which exist here. Gold and silver are parted by salt cementation instead.
- **Saltpetre from nitre beds** [`saltpetre_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/saltpetre_production.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Trap: Latin nitrum means natron (soda), not saltpetre. The white crust on stable and cellar walls is unrecognised. Nitre beds need over a year; no known use creates demand.
- **Chemical elements and conservation of mass** [`chemical_elements`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/chemical_elements.md) — K0, use wrong, make medium, accept low. Four elements (Empedocles, Aristotle, the Stoics) or Epicurean atoms without chemistry. Goldsmiths and the mint weigh well, but nobody weighs before and after burning. Local: mint at the temple of Juno Moneta; goldsmiths and assayers.
- **Atomic theory and fixed proportions** [`atomic_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/atomic_theory.md) — K2, use none, make hard, accept medium. Atoms are respectable Epicurean philosophy: Lucretius' poem is recent and Asclepiades built his medicine on particles and pores. Nobody links atoms to fixed weight ratios; that needs pure substances. Local: Lucretius, De rerum natura; Philodemus at Herculaneum; Roman Epicureans (Atticus, Cassius).

- **Gas laws (pressure, volume, temperature)** [`gas_laws`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gas_laws.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Ctesibius' and Philo's books on pneumatics show that air is a body and can be compressed. No barometer and no sealed glass tubes. - **Collecting and telling apart gases (hydrogen, fixed air)** [`pneumatic_chemistry_gases`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pneumatic_chemistry_gases.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Deadly vapours at volcanic vents near Puteoli and at Ampsanctus are known as breath of the underworld. There is one air; kinds of air is a new thought.
- **Acids, alkalis and indicators** [`acids_bases_ph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/acids_bases_ph.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Vinegar is the only acid, natron and ash lye the alkalis; they are known to fizz together. Plant juices that change colour (violets, red cabbage) are an easy demonstration.

Natron (nitrum) comes from Egypt for glass, cleaning and medicine; wood-ash lye is a household thing. Making lye caustic with quicklime is not practised. Elsewhere: Egypt, Wadi Natrun.
- **Lime burning and lime mortar** [`lime_burning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lime_burning.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Cato (De agri cultura 38) gives the dimensions of a lime kiln. Lime burnt from limestone and travertine is the basis of all building mortar. Local: lime burners (calcarii); Cato, De agri cultura 38.
- **Salt making (sea salt, brine boiling, rock salt)** [`salt_production`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/salt_production.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Sea salt from evaporation pans at the Tiber mouth, carried inland on the Via Salaria. Salt is a state concern and cheap. Local: salt pans at Ostia; Via Salaria.
- **Dyeing with mordants and vat dyes** [`mordant_dyeing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mordant_dyeing.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Dyers use alum and iron mordants with madder, weld, woad and shellfish purple. Indigo arrives only as a costly Indian pigment. Caesar's new law restricts purple garments. Local: alum from Lipari; dyers (infectores) and purple sellers (purpurarii). Elsewhere: Tyre, shellfish purple; India, indigo and mordant-dyed cotton.
